```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#Define custom functions
#AMOVA permutation test (amova.fn / randamova.fn from my_functions): draws the null histogram, optionally saves it to
#'file', and returns the observed statistic and p-value (amovapval.fn only plots). p = proportion of permutations >= observed.
#Note: amova.fn's statistic has a ~0.5 baseline, so only the p-value is interpretable.
amova_test=function(distmat,cell_key,iterations=30000,plottitle="",file=NULL,seed=20261031){
  groupnames=unique(cell_key$Cell_type)
  set.seed(seed)
  obs=amova.fn(distmat=distmat,groupnames=groupnames,cell_key=cell_key)
  rnd=sapply(1:iterations,function(i) randamova.fn(distmat=distmat,groupnames=groupnames,cell_key=cell_key))
  p=mean(rnd>=obs)
  draw=function(){
    hist(rnd,col="grey",100,main=plottitle,xlab="AMOVA statistic",xlim=range(c(rnd,obs)))
    abline(v=obs,col="red",lwd=2)
    legend("topright",legend=paste0("Observed\n p = ",signif(p,digits=2)),lwd=2,col="red",bty="n")
  }
  draw()
  if(!is.null(file)) {pdf(file,width=5,height=4); draw(); dev.off()}
  data.frame(n_colonies=nrow(distmat),statistic=obs,null_mean=mean(rnd),p_value=p,iterations=iterations)
}
#Clades whose branch crosses a given height (from the HSCT analysis scripts)
get_expanded_clade_nodes=function(tree,height_cut_off=100,min_clonal_fraction=0.02,min_samples=1){
  nodeheights=nodeHeights(tree)
  nodes=tree$edge[,2][nodeheights[,1] < height_cut_off &
                        !nodeheights[,2] < height_cut_off &
                        sapply(tree$edge[,2],function(node) {length(getTips(tree,node))/length(tree$tip.label)})>min_clonal_fraction &
                        sapply(tree$edge[,2],function(node) {length(getTips(tree,node))})>=min_samples]
  data.frame(nodes=nodes,n_samples=sapply(nodes,function(node) {length(getTips(tree,node))}),
             MRCA_time=sapply(nodes,function(node) {nodeheight(tree,node)}),
             clonal_fraction=sapply(nodes,function(node) {length(getTips(tree,node))/length(tree$tip.label)}))
}

plot_96profile=function(df,colnames=c("sampleID","chr","pos","ref","alt"),genomeFile,title=NULL) {
  require(Rsamtools)
  require(GenomicRanges)
  require(IRanges)
  mutations = data.frame(sampleID=df[[colnames[1]]],
                         chr=df[[colnames[2]]],
                         pos=df[[colnames[3]]],
                         ref=df[[colnames[4]]],
                         trinuc_ref= "-",
                         mut=df[[colnames[5]]])
  mutations_GRange<-GRanges(mutations$chr, IRanges::IRanges(mutations$pos-1, mutations$pos+1))
  mutations$trinuc_ref = as.vector(Rsamtools::scanFa(file=genomeFile,mutations_GRange ))
  
  ntcomp = c(T="A",G="C",C="G",A="T")
  mutations$sub = paste(mutations$ref,mutations$mut,sep=">")
  mutations$trinuc_ref_py = mutations$trinuc_ref
  for (j in 1:nrow(mutations)) {
    if (mutations$ref[j] %in% c("A","G")) { # Purine base
      mutations$sub[j] = paste(ntcomp[mutations$ref[j]],ntcomp[mutations$mut[j]],sep=">")
      mutations$trinuc_ref_py[j] = paste(ntcomp[rev(strsplit(mutations$trinuc_ref[j],split="")[[1]])],collapse="")
    }
  }
  freqs = table(paste(mutations$sub,paste(substr(mutations$trinuc_ref_py,1,1),substr(mutations$trinuc_ref_py,3,3),sep="-"),sep=","))
  sub_vec = c("C>A","C>G","C>T","T>A","T>C","T>G")
  ctx_vec = paste(rep(c("A","C","G","T"),each=4),rep(c("A","C","G","T"),times=4),sep="-")
  full_vec = paste(rep(sub_vec,each=16),rep(ctx_vec,times=6),sep=",")
  freqs_full = freqs[full_vec]; freqs_full[is.na(freqs_full)] = 0; names(freqs_full) = full_vec
  
  xstr = paste(substr(full_vec,5,5), substr(full_vec,1,1), substr(full_vec,7,7), sep="")
  
  #pdf("Mut_Sig_fetal_shared.pdf")
  colvec = rep(c("dodgerblue","black","red","grey70","olivedrab3","plum2"),each=16)
  y = freqs_full; maxy = max(y)
  h = barplot(y, las=2, col=colvec, border=NA, ylim=c(0,maxy*1.5), space=1, cex.names=0.6, names.arg=xstr, ylab="Number mutations",main=title)
  for (j in 1:length(sub_vec)) {
    xpos = h[c((j-1)*16+1,j*16)]
    rect(xpos[1]-0.5, maxy*1.2, xpos[2]+0.5, maxy*1.3, border=NA, col=colvec[j*16])
    text(x=mean(xpos), y=maxy*1.3, pos=3, label=sub_vec[j])
  }
}

plot_96profile_mutref=function(mutref_vec,genomeFile,title=NULL) {
  mut_mat=stringr::str_split(mutref_vec,pattern="-",simplify=T)
  colnames(mut_mat)=c("chr","pos","ref","alt")
  df=as.data.frame(mut_mat)%>%
    mutate(pos=as.integer(pos))%>%
    mutate(sampleID="this_sample",.before=1)
  plot_96profile(df,genomeFile = genomeFile,title=title)
}

vaf_density_plot_final=function(sample,tree,COMB_mats,private_only=F){
  node <- which(tree$tip.label==sample)
  if(private_only) {relevant_nodes<-node} else {relevant_nodes<-get_ancestral_nodes(node,tree$edge)}
  sample_muts <- COMB_mats$mat$mut_ref[COMB_mats$mat$node %in% relevant_nodes]
  COMB_mats$NR[COMB_mats$NR == 0] <- 1
  dens <- density((COMB_mats$NV/COMB_mats$NR)[sample_muts,sample])
  plot(dens,xlim = c(0,1),main=sample)
  abline(v = dens$x[which.max(dens$y)])
  text(0.7, max(dens$y) - 0.2, paste("Peak VAF dens=",round(dens$x[which.max(dens$y)], digits = 2)),col="red",cex = 0.7)
}

binom_mix = function(x,size,nrange=1:3,criterion="BIC",maxit=5000,tol=1e-6){
  ## Perform the EM algorithm for different numbers of components
  ## Select best fit using the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC)
  ## or the Akaike information criterion (AIC)
  i=1
  results = list()
  BIC_vec = c()
  AIC_vec = c()
  
  for (n in nrange){
    ## Initialise EM algorithm with values from kmeans clustering
    init = kmeans(x/size,n)
    prop_init = init$size/length(x)
    p_init = init$centers
    
    results[[i]] = em.algo(x,size,prop.vector_inits = prop_init,p.vector_inits=p_init,nclust=n,maxit,tol)
    BIC_vec = c(BIC_vec,results[[i]]$BIC)
    AIC_vec = c(AIC_vec,results[[i]]$AIC)
    i=i+1
  }
  if (criterion=="BIC"){
    results[[which.min(BIC_vec)]]$BIC_vec=BIC_vec
    return(results[[which.min(BIC_vec)]])
  }
  if (criterion=="AIC"){
    return(results[[which.min(AIC_vec)]])
  }
}
```

## Plot trees with tissue source info

In this plot, branches are coloured by the specific tissue colour if all the descendants are from the same tissue.
If descendants come from different tissues, the colour is black.

```{r plot_source,fig.width=12, fig.height=5}

#Can choose the 
plot_sharing_multiple=function(tree,details,matrices,node,cat_df,cat_name="cat",sharing_cols=c("dark green","red","orange","brown","green"),...){  
  library(dplyr)
  categories=cat_df%>%filter(sample%in%tree$tip.label)%>%pull(cat_name)%>%unique()
  if(length(categories)>length(sharing_cols)) {stop("Not enough colours supplied for number of categories")}
  info=get_edge_info(tree,details,node=node)
  sample_categories=cat_df%>%filter(sample%in%info$samples)%>%pull(cat_name)
  if(length(unique(sample_categories))>1) {
    sharing_info <- "shared"
  } else {
    sharing_info <- unique(sample_categories)
  }
  sharing_cols=sharing_cols[1:length(categories)]
  
  #Add black as the first "shared" category colour
  if(all(categories%in%names(sharing_cols))) {
    sharing_cols<-sharing_cols[categories]
    sharing_cols<-c("black",sharing_cols)
    names(sharing_cols)[1]="shared"
  } else {
    sharing_cols<-c("black",sharing_cols)
    names(sharing_cols)=c("shared",categories)
  }
  
  if(length(tree$edge.length[tree$edge[,2]==node])>0){
    arrows(y0=info$yb,y1=info$yt,x0=info$x,x1=info$x,length=0,col=sharing_cols[sharing_info],lend=1,...)
  }
}
```

### Correct branch lengths for sensitivity and sub-clonal private mutations

Private mutations include sub-clonal mutations (acquired after the founder cell, VAF ~0.25) and not every clonal mutation is detected. The correction (`burden_correction/`, see its README for the method and a simulation test) accounts for how mutations reach the tree:

1. A private mutation is only on the tree if NV >= 3 and VAF >= 0.2 (tree-building filter), and calls with exactly 3 variant reads are only partly detected. Sub-clonal mutations are therefore lost far more often at low depth, so the clonal/sub-clonal mixture is fitted *conditional on detection* (beta-binomial clonal and sub-clonal components shared across colonies, a clonal weight per colony).
2. Male X/Y mutations are hemizygous (VAF ~1 at half depth) and are modelled with twice the VAF.
3. Clonal sensitivity = the pipeline's germline-SNP sensitivity (recovered from the input tree: tip SNV count / tip edge length) x the probability that a clonal mutation passes the VAF filter at that sample's depth.
4. Corrected private branch = expected number of detected clonal SNVs / clonal sensitivity. Shared branches are rebuilt from raw SNV counts and divided by the probability that at least one descendant sample detects a mutation.

In simulations with known truth this is within +-2% of the true clonal burden (the previous Bayesian hard-call correction underestimated it by 8-27%, depending on depth). The fit is saved in `burden_correction/results/` and reloaded if present.

```{r burden_correction}
bc_file=paste0(my_working_dir,"burden_correction/results/burden_correction_",sample_ID,".Rds")

} else {
  bc=correct_branch_lengths(tree=read.tree(paste0(my_working_dir,"tree_files/tree_",sample_ID,"_postMS_reduced_a_j_vaf_post_mix_post_dup.tree")),
                            COMB_mats=filtered_muts$COMB_mats.tree.build,sex="male")
}

#Fitted global parameters
data.frame(clonal_VAF=unname(bc$fit$pc),subclonal_VAF=unname(bc$fit$ps),rho_clonal=bc$fit$rho[1],rho_subclonal=bc$fit$rho[2],
           detection_NV3=bc$fit$delta[1],detection_NV4=bc$fit$delta[2])%>%signif(3)

#Per-sample: observed private SNVs, clonal weight, sensitivity and corrected burdens

  left_join(sample_level_metadata,by=c("sample"="INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME"))%>%
```

### Make a new ultrametric tree with the corrected mutation burdens

This uses the 'make.ultrametric.tree' function which is an iteratively reweighted means algorithm to scale the total sample heights all to a height of 1. We then rescale them to the mean mutation burden across samples. This gives an ultrametric tree that is still scaled to 'molecular time' (i.e. number of mutations). \

You can then look for phylogenetic clustering by tissue using AMOVA, and for differences in tissue composition between the clades present at successive molecular-time cut-offs (chi-squared test with Monte Carlo p-values).

```{r corrected_ultrametric_tree}
tree.corrected.ultra=make.ultrametric.tree(tree.corrected)
tree.corrected.ultra$coords<-NULL
tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length[is.infinite(tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length)]<-0
tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length<-tree.corrected.ultra$edge.length*mean(get_mut_burden(tree.corrected))
tree.corrected.ultra=plot_tree(tree.corrected.ultra,cex.label=0,plot_axis = T,title = sample_ID)

#Apply the 'plot_sharing_multiple' function to colour the branches
temp=add_annotation(tree=tree.corrected.ultra,
               annot_function=plot_sharing_multiple,
               cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
               cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE",
               lwd=2,
               sharing_cols=cell_type_colours)

#Apply the 'plot_category_tip_point' function to create coloured tips according to the tissue
temp=sapply(tree.corrected.ultra$tip.label,function(sample_ID) plot_category_tip_point(sample_ID = sample_ID,
                                                                  tree=tree.corrected.ultra, cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
                                                                  cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE",
                                                                  cols=cell_type_colours,
                                                                  cex=1))

#Plot the legend
legend("topleft", inset=c(.01,.01), title="Sample type",
       names(cell_type_colours), fill=cell_type_colours, horiz=F, cex=0.7)

#Repeat the AMOVA with this version of the tree, though
cellkey<-sample_level_metadata%>%
  dplyr::mutate("Sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME)%>%
  dplyr::filter(Sample%in%tree.corrected.ultra$tip.label)%>%
```

```{r figure_tree_and_chisq}
cell_type_colours=c("#219EBC","#023047","#FFB703", "#FB8500")
names(cell_type_colours)<-unique(sample_level_metadata$TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)
cell_type_colours<-cell_type_colours[which(names(cell_type_colours)%in%(sample_level_metadata%>%dplyr::filter(INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME%in%tree$tip.label)%>%pull(TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)))]

#Apply the 'plot_sharing_multiple' function to colour the branches
temp=add_annotation(tree=tree.ultra,
               annot_function=plot_sharing_multiple,
               cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
               cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE",
               lwd=3,
               sharing_cols=cell_type_colours)

#Apply the 'plot_category_tip_point' function to create coloured tips according to the tissue
temp=sapply(tree.ultra$tip.label,function(sample_ID) plot_category_tip_point(sample_ID = sample_ID,
                                                                  tree=tree.ultra, cat_df=sample_level_metadata%>%mutate("sample"=INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME),
                                                                  cat_name="TISSUE_PHENOTYPE",
                                                                  cols=cell_type_colours,
                                                                  cex=1))

#Plot the legend
legend("topleft", inset=c(.01,.01), title="Sample type",
       names(cell_type_colours), fill=cell_type_colours, horiz=F, cex=0.7)
save_base_plot(paste0(sample_ID,"_tree_corrected_ultrametric"),width=10,height=5)

#Clade x tissue contingency test at each molecular-time cut-off: does tissue composition differ between the lineages
#crossing that height? All lineages are included, single colonies too, so the table partitions all colonies and the
#Monte Carlo p-value (margins fixed) is a permutation test of bone labels across colonies. With the margins fixed the
#single colonies only add a constant to the statistic, which is a weighted count of different-bone pairs within clades.
#Excluding them (as before 2026-11-03) only compared clades with each other, missing clades that all share the same
#bone bias. NA if < 2 lineages
set.seed(1)
cutoff_vec<-seq(1,60,1)
tissues<-sample_level_metadata%>%filter(INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME%in%tree.ultra$tip.label)%>%pull(TISSUE_PHENOTYPE)%>%unique()
chisq.res<-lapply(cutoff_vec,function(height) {
  clades_df<-get_expanded_clade_nodes(tree=tree.ultra, height_cut_off = height,min_clonal_fraction = 0,min_samples = 1)
  clade_nodes<-clades_df%>%filter(n_samples>0)%>%pull(nodes)
  if(length(clade_nodes)<2) return(list(p.value=NA,n_clades=length(clade_nodes)))
  
  #Create the anatomy matrix (clades x tissues)
  M<-t(sapply(clade_nodes,function(node) {
    clade_samples<-getTips(tree.ultra,node)
    table(factor(sample_level_metadata%>%filter(INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME%in%clade_samples)%>%pull(TISSUE_PHENOTYPE),levels=tissues))
  }))
  M<-M[,colSums(M)>0,drop=F]
  if(ncol(M)<2) return(list(p.value=NA,n_clades=nrow(M)))
  res<-chisq.test(M,simulate.p.value=TRUE,B=10000)
  list(p.value=res$p.value,n_clades=nrow(M))
})

chisq_df<-data.frame(molecular_time=cutoff_vec,
                     n_clades=sapply(chisq.res,function(res) res$n_clades),
                     chisq.p.value=sapply(chisq.res,function(res) res$p.value))%>%
  mutate(signif=chisq.p.value<0.05)
#Note: the cut-offs are nested and correlated, and the p-values are not corrected for multiple testing
chisq_by_moltime_plot<-chisq_df%>%filter(!is.na(chisq.p.value))%>%
  ggplot(aes(y=molecular_time,x=chisq.p.value,colour = signif))+
  geom_point(size = 0.7)+
  theme_classic()+
  scale_color_manual(values=c("black","#E31A1C"),guide="none")+
  geom_vline(xintercept=0.05,linetype=2)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,1,0.1),limits = c(0,1),position="top")+
  labs(y="Molecular time cut-off",x=expression(chi^2~"p-value for anatomical clustering"))+
  scale_y_reverse(breaks = seq(0,max(cutoff_vec),10))+
  my_theme
chisq_by_moltime_plot
save_gg(chisq_by_moltime_plot,paste0(sample_ID,"_chisq_by_moltime_plot"),width=3,height=2)
```

```{r chisq_global_test}
#One test across cut-offs (the per-cut-off p-values above are not corrected for testing many nested cut-offs).
#Statistic: the smallest per-cut-off tail probability over cut-offs 5-55 (step 5). Null: bone labels permuted across
#colonies (the same null as the per-cut-off Monte Carlo test); per-cut-off tail probabilities and the distribution of
#the minimum are both taken from the same 2000 permutations.
set.seed(20261103)
global_cuts<-seq(5,55,5)
tip_bone<-setNames(sample_level_metadata$TISSUE_PHENOTYPE,sample_level_metadata$INTERNAL_CASM_SAMPLE_NAME)[tree.ultra$tip.label]
#Lineage of each colony at each cut-off (all lineages crossing the cut-off, as above)
lineage_at<-lapply(global_cuts,function(height){
  nodes<-get_expanded_clade_nodes(tree=tree.ultra,height_cut_off=height,min_clonal_fraction=0,min_samples=1)$nodes
  id<-rep(NA_integer_,length(tip_bone))
  for(k in seq_along(nodes)) id[match(getTips(tree.ultra,nodes[k]),tree.ultra$tip.label)]<-k
  id})
pearson_X2<-function(bone) sapply(lineage_at,function(id){
  M<-table(id,factor(bone,levels=tissues)); M<-M[,colSums(M)>0,drop=F]
  if(nrow(M)<2|ncol(M)<2) return(NA)
  E<-outer(rowSums(M),colSums(M))/sum(M); sum((M-E)^2/E)})
obs_X2<-pearson_X2(tip_bone)
labelled<-!is.na(tip_bone)  #the zero-length "Ancestral" outgroup tip has no bone and is in no lineage
null_X2<-t(replicate(2000,{b<-tip_bone; b[labelled]<-sample(b[labelled]); pearson_X2(b)}))
tail_prob<-function(x) sapply(seq_along(global_cuts),function(i) mean(null_X2[,i]>=x[i]))
use<-which(!is.na(obs_X2))
obs_min<-min(tail_prob(obs_X2)[use])
null_min<-apply(null_X2,1,function(x) min(tail_prob(x)[use]))
global_chisq<-data.frame(sample_ID=sample_ID,cut_offs="5-55 (step 5)",smallest_tail_prob=obs_min,
                         best_cut_off=global_cuts[use][which.min(tail_prob(obs_X2)[use])],
                         global_p=(sum(null_min<=obs_min)+1)/(length(null_min)+1))  #(k+1)/(n+1): never 0
global_chisq
```
